Mervin founded: 1977 by Mike Olson and Pete Saari [6] 14. Mervin is the longest running and last major board building factory in the USA [6] 15. Environmental manufacturing: Zero hazardous waste production [5] 16. Sustainability – energy: Washington State electricity is 89.6% hydroelectric; factory heating runs on renewable biodiesel [7] 17. Sustainability – wood: FSC certified fast growing renewable forest products; finger joining to maximize wood yield; sawdust recycled as soil [7] 18. Sustainability – printing: Eco sublimation printing process creates zero hazardous waste (no toxic silk screen process) [8] 19. Gender: Men's [9] 20. Predecessor model: New model for 2025-2026 season (no direct predecessor — this is GNU's newest all mountain freestyle board) [4] SHAPE & PROFILE 21. Shape: Directional Twin [1] 22. Shape description (twin symmetry): Twin shape is perfectly symmetrical for a balanced ride so you can spin and stomp with outstanding stability whether riding regular or switch [10] 23. Shape description (directional twin): Nose is the same shape and rise as the tail with binding inserts set back for more surface area in the nose [11] 24. Camber type: C3 [1] 25. Camber description (manufacturer): Very mild rocker between your feet with powerful camber to the tip and tail — Mervin's version of traditional camber [12] 26. Camber description (detailed): Aggressive camber-dominant shape with mild rocker between the feet offers explosive pop, stable edge control, and park landing precision [13] 27. C3 profile description: Camber is the traditional profile, popular among high-level park and pipe riders because it offers maximum energy and pop [14] 28. Setback: 0.5 inches (all sizes) — merchant verified [MV] FLEX 29. DISAGREEMENT — Flex rating (manufacturer spec table on gnu.com): 8/10 (Flex 10 = Firm scale) [1] 30. DISAGREEMENT — Flex rating (merchant/Melbourne Snowboard Centre): 6/10 (1=soft, 10=stiff) [15] 31. COMMENT on flex disagreement: The official GNU spec table on gnu.com lists the flex as 8 out of 10, while the merchant site (Melbourne Snowboard Centre) lists it as 6/10. The merchant-supplied attributes also list 6/10. Zumiez describes it as "medium to firm flex rating" [3], and Snowboarder.com says "softer flex pattern" [4]. Snowboard International says "stiff flex" [16]. These discrepancies likely arise from different scaling systems or subjective interpretation. The manufacturer spec table (8/10) should be treated as authoritative for the product specification. 32. Flex description (Zumiez): Medium to firm flex rating [3] 33. Flex description (Snowboard International): Stiff flex [16] 34. Flex description (Snowboarder magazine): Softer flex pattern [4] 35. Flex description (Melbourne Snowboard Centre): Mid-flex, balanced blend of flexibility and stiffness — merchant verified [15] 36. Flex feel (snowboards.eu): The board feels solid and powerful underfoot, yet retains enough forgiveness for progressive freestyle movements [17] CONSTRUCTION & MATERIALS 37. Core material: G Lite 2 Core — FSC certified Aspen and Paulownia wood [5] 38. Core description: Light, strong, and poppy [5] 39. Forestry certification: FSC (Forest Stewardship Council) certified [5] 40. Laminate: Tri-Ax/Bi-Ax fiberglass + Carbon Power Bands [5] 41. Laminate description: Enhanced flex energy return and torsional stability for powerful turns and landings [13] 42. Carbon reinforcement: Carbon Power Bands [5] 43. Carbon description: Add pop, response, and extend lifespan [15] 44. Sidewall material: UHMW (Ultra High Molecular Weight Polyethylene) [5] 45. UHMW description: Strong, durable, and resistant to abrasion, chemicals, and impact [15] 46. Topsheet: Eco Sublimated Poly Topsheet [5] 47. Topsheet description: Tough and environmentally nice [5] 48. DISAGREEMENT — Base type (manufacturer & evo — "Co-Ex"): Eco Sublimated Co-Ex Base — fast, tough, and holds wax [5] 49. DISAGREEMENT — Base type (Absolute-Snow & Snowboard International — "Sintered"): Eco-sublimated sintered base ensures speed and wax retention [18] 50. COMMENT on base disagreement: GNU's own site and evo both list the base as "Co-Ex" (co-extruded/extruded), while Absolute-Snow, Snowboard International, and super-shop.com describe it as "sintered." Co-extruded (extruded) and sintered are different manufacturing processes. The manufacturer site (GNU.com) is authoritative, so the base should be considered Co-Ex (extruded). Third-party sites appear to have made an error. Melbourne Snowboard Centre confirms: "This base is made of a fast and tough extruded material" [19], supporting the manufacturer. 51. Base description: Fast, tough, easy to maintain [5] 52. Base is wax-retentive [13] 53. Construction: Wet laminated with proprietary epoxy formula, pressed in custom formblocks [20] 54. Edge technology: Magne-Traction® [5] 55. Magne-Traction description: 7 strategically located and sized edge serrations provide unreal edge hold and control in all conditions [5] 56.
